pick.headline: Grenada's Maurice Bishop is placed under house arrest
pick.summary: On October 13, 1983, a faction of Grenada's ruling New Jewel Movement led by Deputy Prime Minister Bernard Coard placed Prime Minister Maurice Bishop under house arrest.
pick.significance: The split ended with Bishop's execution on October 19. Six days later U.S. forces invaded Grenada, citing the safety of American medical students and the island's ties to Cuba.
pick.fbis: The Latin America report of October 17, 1983, listed a run of Grenada items in its contents: Bishop Under House Arrest, Coard Resigns Position, a state of uncertainty, Radix arrested, protests and journalists expelled, with Barbados urging Bishop's release.

alternates.headline: Oscar Arias wins the Nobel Peace Prize
alternates.summary: On October 13, 1987, the Nobel Committee awarded the Peace Prize to Costa Rican President Oscar Arias for his Central American peace plan, signed by five presidents at Esquipulas, Guatemala, that August.
alternates.significance: The prize strengthened the regional peace process at a time when the Reagan administration was still seeking aid for the Nicaraguan contras, and the plan became the framework for ending the wars in Nicaragua and later El Salvador.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America report of October 14, 1987, carried a Nicaraguan official's remarks on the Esquipulas II peace process, in which he congratulated Costa Rican President Arias on the Nobel Peace Prize as world recognition of the plan.
